turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the system's crawling, just give me a second while this file opens. What brings you in?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, doctor, it's this tummy, and I want to explain it properly so you have the whole picture. Since my niece's wedding I've had the runs and I've been vomiting, and it's knocked me sideways.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm his carer, I stay at the flat during the week. He's been up and down to the loo all night, so I brought him to the rooms this morning already.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the screen jumped back to someone else's notes. Wedding, you said? Say that part again.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturday, in Pietermaritzburg, reception at the hotel. Big buffet, chicken, prawns, potato salad that sat out a while, and we only drove back on Sunday.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. When did the diarrhoea and the vomiting actually start?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): The vomiting started Sunday night, just after we got home, two or three times. The diarrhoea started early Monday morning, and today being Wednesday that's two days of the runs properly.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The vomiting was Sunday night and a bit of yesterday morning. He hasn't thrown up since about ten yesterday.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, the vomiting has stopped. It's the diarrhoea that's still going, my mouth is dry, and I felt wobbly when I stood up this morning.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many times have you been with the diarrhoea?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I tried to keep a tally on a bit of paper and then the paper got wet, which is disgusting, I know. Yesterday I reckon six or seven, this morning already three, and then I lost count after the garage, so I wouldn't swear to a total.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool, or black stool?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no blood, and it's not black. It's watery and brown, and it smells like that prawn dish, sorry.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you feel feverish or shivery at all?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose I felt a bit warm in the night, sometimes, not really. I never took my temperature, so I can't say I had a fever.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that once more, an email just popped over the notes.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I felt a bit warm, sometimes, not really a fever. I didn't check with a thermometer.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll leave that then. Cramps in the tummy?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, low down, they come just before I have to run, mild I'd say. They ease off once I've been, and then they build again, it's a rotten cycle.
[SEG0020] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He also told me his mouth was dry and he went dizzy getting up for water. I made him sit on the bed.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you taken anything for the diarrhoea?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped at the chemist by the robot yesterday, and the lady said if it's a bug maybe don't take a stopper, but I bought the loperamide anyway. Two milligram capsules, I took two to start, then one after each loose stool, four capsules altogether since yesterday afternoon.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Four capsules, say it again, I typed two by mistake.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Two milligrams in each capsule. Two capsules to start, then one after a stool, four in total since yesterday afternoon, and none this morning.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the loperamide. If this is infectious you want it out, not held in, so no more of those capsules.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I did tell him the chemist said leave it, but he worries about being caught short away from the flat.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else from that wedding been ill?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister phoned, she and her husband both vomited on Monday, and my cousin says three people at their table have the runs. I'm convinced it was the prawns, though the potato salad was in the sun too, I watched it.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any ongoing illnesses, diabetes, bowel problems?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, and no Crohn's or colitis or anything like that. I had my appendix out at twenty-two, ages ago, and I take a blood pressure tablet every day.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which tablet, what dose? The medication list here is empty, typical.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine, five milligrams, one every morning, for years now. I took today's with a sip of water, I didn't miss it.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines or foods?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all. I've had penicillin in the past and I was fine, and foods are fine too.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He does get heartburn if he eats late, but that's an old thing, not this week, and it's not why we came.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tongue's dry, lips are dry, and the skin on the hand tents slightly then springs back, so that's mild dehydration. Tummy is soft, mildly tender low down, no guarding.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Machine says pulse 98, blood pressure 112 over 70, temperature 36.9. Saturation is 98 percent, I'm not fussed about that.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 98 bad? My heart thumps on the stairs at the flat anyway, and I hardly slept because the neighbour's dog barked till late, which is a whole story about the body corporate.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): 98 is a touch fast and it fits with being dry and awake all night. I'm not opening the dog story.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's only managed small sips, and he skipped supper. Breakfast was two biscuits and that was a push.

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thinking aloud, this could be food poisoning off that buffet, or a viral gastroenteritis the bunch of you caught together. I'm not going to decide which, and I won't call it settled today.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): No stool test today. If you're still having watery stools on Friday, then we'll send a sample off, not before.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Friday, all right, and do I get a little bottle from the lab or from you? Also I park badly at these rooms, the bay is tiny, but that's not your problem.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): The lab gives the pot, only if we get to that point. For now, fluids. Sip rehydration solution, a Rehidrat sachet in a glass of water, little and often, plain food if you're hungry, nothing rich, and leave the loperamide alone.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Rehidrat, the orange sachets? I think there's a box at home from last summer, though I couldn't tell you if it's expired, I never check dates properly.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The box is in the cupboard and I don't trust the date on it. I'll buy a fresh one at the chemist on the way.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the inbox flashed, how many sachets did I say? One sachet to a glass, sip through the day, and try to get through at least a litre if you can manage it.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): A litre, got it. I've got Buscopan at home, hyoscine, ten milligrams, but I haven't taken any this week, I picked the box up and put it down again.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave the Buscopan, you haven't used it and the cramps are mild. They should ease as the tummy settles.
[SEG0050] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And if he starts vomiting again tonight? He went very pale on Sunday, I didn't like it.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the vomiting comes back and he can't keep fluids down, or he gets more dizzy, or there's blood, come back sooner. If the diarrhoea is still going on Friday, come back and we'll do the stool then.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): So Friday only if I'm still running, otherwise I stay at the flat and drink, and I work from home on Thursdays so the bathroom is right there down the passage.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's the plan. You get the new Rehidrat and watch the sips, and I'll wrestle these notes once the screen stops freezing.

spec.situation: Diarrhoea and vomiting after a trip or a wedding meal; others at the event are ill; patient counts bowel movements loosely; takes loperamide against advice; mild dehydration signs; stool test conditional; advice on fluids.
features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Use is reported, but status not current now; doctor told him to stop and none taken this morning.
